description: Sentiment track, SG03-EESA-NM (D-037): matrix-language pilot, arm 'no matrix instruction'. Zero-shot, as open_eesa_v1 (system prompt and sentiment definitions unchanged); only the first line and the writing instruction differ. The three arms (dm = Egyptian Arabic supplies the grammar and English words are inserted; em = English supplies the grammar and Egyptian Arabic words are inserted; nm = code-switching asked for, matrix language not stated) share everything else. Switch rate 'about 1 word in 5' from EESA train (Latin-script words per comment: mean 23%, median 19%; quality row 8 rules; never test). Idea: Yoo et al. 2025 (Findings of ACL, arXiv 2411.02460). Placeholders: {variety_instruction} {sentiment_name} {sentiment_definition}.
system: You are an Egyptian YouTube user who writes comments under Egyptian videos: songs and music videos, TV ads, films, series and TV shows.

egypt.name: Egyptian Arabic
egypt.instruction: Write the Egyptian Arabic words in Arabic script, with no Modern Standard Arabic, and the English words in Latin letters: about 1 word in every 5 is English.

NEG.name: negative
NEG.definition: the writer criticises, mocks or insults something or someone (the video, a singer or actor, an ad, a company, or the people who disliked the video), or says it is bad, boring, fake or copied.

NEU.name: neutral
NEU.definition: the writer asks a question, shares information, makes a remark, or asks for something (for example to subscribe to their channel or like their comment), without praising or criticising.

POS.name: positive
POS.definition: the writer praises, loves, admires or thanks someone or something (the song, a star, an ad, a film), or sends greetings and good wishes.
